On Mar 28, 2019, at 9:30 PM, Allen Schweitzer alvie00@yahoo.com [ballyalley] <ballyalley@yahoogroups.com> wrote:


  

 Anybody with a working unit should replace their C1, C6 and C10, in my humble opinion.  When I sell a unit, I also replace C 7, 8, 13 and 62.  I learned to do this after chasing a 5V problem to C8 once or twice with Ken's help.  I figure it's best to do them all.    I also replace C 63 and 64, unless I socket and replace the RAM's with 4164's.  In that case, I just pull C 63 and 64 out and place them next to the 12V regulator in the trash can.  That makes 3 parts that can't fail and ruin your Ballynjoyment.  :)  If you're going to replace your RAM's with 4164's, there's a bit more to it than that.  I can write that up if anyone is interested.

I use 22uf 50V for 7, 62, 63 and 64.  I'm currently using 10uf for C8.  The service manual calls for 6.8uf.  When I run out of 10's, I'll start using the 22uf there as well.  In a lot of the unit's I have recapped, I find a 15uf cap in for C8 from the factory. 

For C1 I use a 2200uf 25V axial, because why not (?), and they also go in the Atari 2600's that I work on occasionally.
For C10, I am currently using a 100uf 25V capacitor, but in speaking with Michael Matte, I have in my mental notes that this capacitor should be on the order of 35V or more.  That change will be made after I run out of 25V'ers.
For C6, I'm currently using a 10V as I found them cheap on e-bay, but again, Michael recommends using 25V or higher (as I remember).  The notes for some of this are on the ballyalley website somewhere.  I'm a poor navigator, so I use my own method of note-keeping to track this as I come across the information.
And I LOVE LOVE LOVE that heat sink Console5 sells.  I've never put it on top of a "factory" heat sink that's already on a data chip, because I'm not sure there's room for the keypad connection.  I've run a Bally for 6 hours using that heat sink, and it never seems to get hot.  That is the ONLY heat sink I will use on a data chip that has no other heat sink.  Don't use it on the address or I/O chip, please.  It's unnecessary, and can only serve to confuse, like the Bally that sold on e-bay a year or 2 ago, that had that heat sinks on all of the customs.  If you ever needed to pull them out, and they get mixed up, good luck not cooking your Bally, and don't call me.  And enjoy your Atomic Fireball (free with every purchase from Console5)!

I'm glad to have joined us here, Tim.  It's always nice to see old-school BASIC programmers for the astrocade drop by this forum.

If the audio from your tapes has already been recorded in lossless digital format, such as WAV or FLAC, then getting the programs to load is probably possible.  Normally, this requires the programs to be run through some tape archiving tools available on ballyalley.com, here:

http://www.ballyalley.com/program_downloads/tape_archive_tools/tape_archive_tools.html

I presume these are 2000-baud recording from "AstroBASIC" (the cart with the built in tape interface).  If that is correct, then you need tools called AstroWAV and Ballybin.

If the audio was saved as a lossy format, such as MP3, then the chances of getting the program to load are near-impossible, even if the tape archiving tools are used.  In that case, you'll need to save the audio again in a non-lossy format.

Lance mentioned adjusting the volume can get files to work from a phone.  I agree with him, with the cavett that this is easily done with files that have already been digitally archived.  Also, there is a "gotcha" when loading files from a phone or iPod.  Usually iTunes automatically will reduce the quality of recording to save storage space on the device.  I can't remember what the setting is called, but this option must be turned off before any audio files that will be reloaded onto the astrocade can be used.

What format is the audio in right now?

Adam

    On Monday, April 1, 2019, 2:23:42 PM EDT, Adam Trionfo ballyalley@hotmail.com [ballyalley] <ballyalley@yahoogroups.com> wrote:

  

I'm glad to have joined us here, Tim.  It's always nice to see old-school BASIC programmers for the astrocade drop by this forum.

If the audio from your tapes has already been recorded in lossless digital format, such as WAV or FLAC, then getting the programs to load is probably possible.  Normally, this requires the programs to be run through some tape archiving tools available on ballyalley.com, here:

http://www.ballyalley.com/program_downloads/tape_archive_tools/tape_archive_tools.html
I presume these are 2000-baud recording from "AstroBASIC" (the cart with the built in tape interface).  If that is correct, then you need tools called AstroWAV and Ballybin.

If the audio was saved as a lossy format, such as MP3, then the chances of getting the program to load are near-impossible, even if the tape archiving tools are used.  In that case, you'll need to save the audio again in a non-lossy format.

Lance mentioned adjusting the volume can get files to work from a phone.  I agree with him, with the cavett that this is easily done with files that have already been digitally archived.  Also, there is a "gotcha" when loading files from a phone or iPod.  Usually iTunes automatically will reduce the quality of recording to save storage space on the device.  I can't remember what the setting is called, but this option must be turned off before any audio files that will be reloaded onto the astrocade can be used.

What format is the audio in right now?

Adam
